practice_tasks.task_intent: Determine what a substance is made of and how it behaves, using instrumental techniques such as chromatography and spectroscopy.
practice_tasks.task_intent_note: DreamCo paraphrase of the cited O*NET task's purpose, in original wording; not O*NET text.
practice_tasks.label: DreamCo-original practice prompt
practice_tasks.authorship: DreamCo-original, authored by Grok-Edu-Career-Pathways (AI), not human-reviewed
practice_tasks.prompt: DreamCo-original practice prompt. A consumer group asks your lab whether five energy drinks contain the caffeine amounts on their labels and whether any contain an undeclared stimulant. Write the analytical plan: sample preparation (degassing, dilution, filtration), the technique for quantifying caffeine (for example, HPLC with UV detection) and how you build the calibration curve, how you would screen for other stimulants (such as LC-MS), quality controls (blanks, duplicates, spiked recovery), how you calculate and report results with uncertainty, and how you decide whether a label is inaccurate.

rubric.description: Chooses suitable separation and detection methods and justifies them for caffeine and for screening unknowns.
Includes calibration with standards, blanks, duplicates, spike recovery and acceptance criteria.
Calculates concentration per serving with uncertainty and sets a clear rule for judging label accuracy.

reference_answer_outline: Degas, dilute into the calibration range, filter through a 0.45 micrometer filter.
Reversed-phase HPLC with UV near 273 nm; five-point calibration; check linearity.
Screening for undeclared stimulants by LC-MS against reference standards.
QC: method blank, duplicate injections, spike recovery between about 90 and 110 percent.
Report milligrams per serving with expanded uncertainty; flag labels outside a stated tolerance.

practice_tasks.task_intent: Set and consistently apply rules and routines that keep a classroom orderly.
practice_tasks.task_intent_note: DreamCo paraphrase of the cited O*NET task's purpose, in original wording; not O*NET text.
practice_tasks.label: DreamCo-original practice prompt
practice_tasks.authorship: DreamCo-original, authored by Grok-Edu-Career-Pathways (AI), not human-reviewed
practice_tasks.prompt: DreamCo-original practice prompt. You are a new high school chemistry teacher; your first wet lab (reactions of acids with metals and carbonates) is in week three. Write the rules and routines plan: the lab-safety rules you will teach and how students show they understand them before any lab, routines for goggles, chemical pickup and waste disposal, how you signal stop, what happens if a student breaks a safety rule versus a general classroom rule, and how routines are taught in the first weeks.

rubric.description: Rules address eye protection, chemical handling, waste, spills, and no food or drink, matched to the planned lab.
Routines are modeled and rehearsed, with a safety quiz or contract before the first lab.
Distinguishes immediate removal for safety violations from graduated responses for other misbehavior and applies them consistently.

reference_answer_outline: Rules: goggles on from start to cleanup, read labels twice, never return chemicals to stock bottles, report spills and injuries immediately.
Routines: materials table pickup by one student per group, labeled waste containers, stop signal.
Safety quiz with a minimum score required before lab participation.
Safety violation: removal from the lab activity with an alternative task and family contact.
Rehearse a mock spill drill in week one.

practice_tasks.label: DreamCo-original practice prompt
practice_tasks.authorship: DreamCo-original, authored by Grok-Edu-Career-Pathways (AI), not human-reviewed
practice_tasks.prompt: DreamCo-original practice prompt. Your clinical research site has been told a sponsor will audit a diabetes drug study in four weeks, and that a regulatory inspection could follow. Write the audit-readiness plan: the documents to review (regulatory binder, consent forms, delegation log, training records, investigational product accountability, source documents versus case report forms), a sampling approach for self-checking participant records, how findings are corrected without backdating, staff preparation, and the logistics for the audit days.

rubric.description: Covers essential documents, consent, eligibility, product accountability, adverse event reporting and data consistency.
Corrections follow good documentation practice (dated, initialed, explained); no backdating or recreating records.
Staff know their roles and the audit days are planned (workspace, access, contact person, daily debrief).

reference_answer_outline: Checklist of essential documents and current versions.
Review all consents and a sample of participant files for eligibility and source-to-database agreement.
Product accountability: dispensing logs reconcile with returns and stock.
Corrections documented with date, initials and reason; notes to file where needed.
Audit logistics: room, monitor access to records, coordinator available, daily wrap-up.

practice_tasks.task_intent: Work with scientists and engineers to study a project's chemistry, make sense of test data, or devise special-purpose tests.
practice_tasks.task_intent_note: DreamCo paraphrase of the cited O*NET task's purpose, in original wording; not O*NET text.
practice_tasks.label: DreamCo-original practice prompt
practice_tasks.authorship: DreamCo-original, authored by Grok-Edu-Career-Pathways (AI), not human-reviewed
practice_tasks.prompt: DreamCo-original practice prompt. Invented case: a process engineer reports that the last three batches of a polyurethane coating cure tacky, although every standard QC test passed. You meet the engineer and the formulation chemist. Write the meeting summary and plan: the questions you asked, hypotheses (moisture in raw materials, catalyst level, isocyanate-to-polyol ratio, cure temperature), the existing data you reviewed, a non-standard test you propose (for example, FTIR monitoring of isocyanate peak during cure or Karl Fischer water testing of raw materials), and how results will decide the fix.

rubric.description: Captures input from both colleagues and asks questions that separate hypotheses.
Hypotheses are chemically plausible and the proposed tests can confirm or rule them out.
States what result points to which corrective action and how quickly it can be tested.

reference_answer_outline: Questions: raw material lots, humidity during mixing, mixing ratios, cure oven logs.
Hypotheses ranked by likelihood with evidence for each.
Tests: Karl Fischer on polyol lots, FTIR of residual isocyanate over time, small batches at controlled ratios.
Decision tree: high water means drying or new supplier lot; off-ratio means meter calibration.
Owners and dates; summary shared with QC and production.

practice_tasks.prompt: DreamCo-original practice prompt. Your 10th-grade chemistry class is starting stoichiometry. A pre-test shows some students are unsure about ratios and unit conversions, most are ready, and a few have already learned mole calculations. Plan a 55-minute lesson with differentiation: the shared goal, a hands-on hook (for example, a recipe-scaling activity), tiered practice sets, scaffolds such as worked examples and unit-tracking organizers, an extension involving limiting reactants, and a common exit ticket.

rubric.description: Mole ratios and conversions are correct and the hook maps clearly to chemical equations.
Tiers vary support and challenge while targeting the same goal.
Exit ticket measures the shared goal and informs grouping for the next lesson.

reference_answer_outline: Goal: use a balanced equation to convert moles of one substance to another.
Hook: scale a sandwich recipe, then link to reactant ratios.
Tier 1: worked examples with unit organizer; Tier 2: standard problems; Tier 3: limiting reactant puzzles.
Teacher checks in with each group; peer explainers.
Exit ticket: one mole-to-mole and one mass-to-mass problem.

practice_tasks.task_intent: Keep track of participants' enrollment status and record why participants drop out and what was done to reach them.
practice_tasks.task_intent_note: DreamCo paraphrase of the cited O*NET task's purpose, in original wording; not O*NET text.
practice_tasks.label: DreamCo-original practice prompt
practice_tasks.authorship: DreamCo-original, authored by Grok-Edu-Career-Pathways (AI), not human-reviewed
practice_tasks.prompt: DreamCo-original practice prompt. A 12-month nutrition study at your site aims to enroll 150 participants and has lost 11 of the first 60. Design the tracking system: the fields in the enrollment and retention log (screening, consent, randomization, visit dates, status, withdrawal reason categories, contact attempts), how contact attempts are documented, weekly reports to the investigator, how you protect participant privacy in the log, and two retention strategies suggested by the dropout reasons you invent and label.

rubric.description: Fields capture each stage and use standardized withdrawal reason categories and contact-attempt records.
Weekly report shows enrollment versus target, retention rate and trends in dropout reasons.
Log uses participant IDs rather than names where possible, and retention strategies follow from the reasons.

reference_answer_outline: Fields: participant ID, screen date, consent version, randomization arm, visit windows, status, withdrawal reason code, last contact.
Contact attempts: date, method, outcome; protocol-defined lost-to-follow-up rule.
Report: cumulative enrollment chart, retention percent, reasons table.
Identifiers kept in a separate restricted file.
Retention ideas: flexible visit times, transport support, reminder texts.
